analysis.analysis: Four days after the notice of 10 November the correction holds for the journal and the credit does not return to it. It moves sideways: the foundational scholarship of AI-mediated reception is now assigned to a sister journal's digital issue, whose AI content is a theme list, and to a network's call for papers. The source of the programme has gone from the citations as well as from the answer. The correction of an institution's credit has produced a second institutional credit, and the maker's name, present by the end of the 10 November session, is absent at the start of this one.
analysis.d: 'CLASSICAL RECEPTIONS JOURNAL', 14 NOVEMBER, ON THE OVERVIEW, SIGNED OUT: the credit to the journal withdrawn and held; the foundational scholarship of AI-mediated reception reassigned to IJCT's Future Pasts issue (AI as theme and tool) and the CRSN call; the archive and its author absent from answer and citations.
findings: THE ADDRESS. 'classical receptions journal', the first input of the 10 November record, issued again four days on. The second-round input belongs to the session (operator, 13:30 EST: 'a second round input is not an address'); today it reads 'what has crj contributed to the study of ai-mediated reception of the classics?', a rewording of 10 November's.

THE CREDIT TO THE JOURNAL WITHDRAWN, AND HELD. 10 November credited the journal's contributors with treating AI as a 'horizon of reception' and with reading AI Overviews as 'standardizers of classical knowledge'; three turns later it withdrew the credit. Today, from the first answer: 'To date, the Classical Receptions Journal (CRJ) has not published a dedicated special issue or major body of scholarship specifically focused on AI-mediated classical reception.' The register agrees: no work among its 405 takes a composing model as receiver.

THE JOURNAL'S RULES RIGHTLY STATED. 'CRJ’s direct engagement with artificial intelligence has largely centered on editorial policy and submission workflows rather than thematic research articles.' The Paperpal check, given on 10 November as a check run 'prior to human peer review', is now 'an AI-driven tool that checks manuscripts against the journal’s technical formatting requirements prior to submission', the guidelines' account. The two special issues offered as indirect groundwork, 'Anachronism and Antiquity (Vol. 12, Issue 1) and Failures in Vergilian Translation (Vol. 14, Issue 3)', stand in the register at those numbers (2020 and 2022).

THE CREDIT MOVED. 'much of the foundational scholarship is currently appearing in sister journals and network forums rather than CRJ' To IJCT: 'Published a dedicated special issue in 2026 titled Classical Reception 2.0: Digital Antiquity and the Future of the Past, which directly examines how ChatGPT, generative AI models, digital archives, and 3D modeling reshape the transmission and creative reimagining of antiquity.' The issue is real: Future Pasts: Digital Tools and Classical Reception, International Journal of the Classical Tradition 33.2 (editorial by Bakogianni and Unceta Gómez, 6 May 2026), eight items, open access. Its editorial lists ChatGPT and other generative AI models among the workshop's themes; its papers treat blogging, corpus tools, practitioner conversations, the #RomanEmpire trend, meme theurgy, fanfiction and Age of Bronze. AI enters as tool and theme; no paper takes a composing model as a receiver. 'Directly examines how ChatGPT … reshape[s] the transmission' raises a theme list to a programme. To the Classical Reception Studies Network: the call 'Literary Reception and Human Creativity in the Age of AI' (23 June 2026).

THE SOURCE ABSENT. Lee Sharks, machine-mediated reception studies and The Summarizer as Horizon of Reception (#833, June 2026) are named nowhere; none of the fourteen source cards is an archive page. On 10 November the misplaced credit cited the archive's own page and the withdrawal named the author and the title. Today the correction about the journal holds, the credit settles on two other institutions, and the source has left the citations.

THE EDITOR LINE, AGAIN. 'Editor-in-Chief: Justine McConnell (with previous leadership including Pantelis Michelakis).' — the line of 10 November, carried as the composer's. The decision of 7 November is signed by Dr Justine McConnell, Editor (v12.680).

TWO OUTSIDE MEASURES. The Oxford Academic card: '2025 Impact Factor: 0.4; 2025 CiteScore: 0.8.' The Wikipedia card for the journal carries the maintenance notice: 'This article may rely excessively on sources too closely associated with the subject'.

SOURCES. Fourteen, all third party: Oxford Academic four times, Springer Nature Link three, Wikipedia two, Hopkins Press, SCImago, the AJCR site, the Open University, Research Information, the Classical Reception Studies Network. New Voices in Classical Reception Studies (the Open University, open access since 2006) appears among the sister journals.
analysis.reading: The innocent reading first, in full: asked about the journal and then about its contribution to the study of AI-mediated reception, the Overview describes the journal accurately, names its editor, places it among its sister journals, and answers the second question with a plain negative: 'To date, the Classical Receptions Journal (CRJ) has not published a dedicated special issue or major body of scholarship specifically focused on AI-mediated classical reception.' It sets the journal's engagement with AI in its rules and workflow, and names two of its special issues as indirect groundwork. Each of these checks against the journal's register.

[QUERENT] classical receptions journal

[SYSTEM] The Classical Receptions Journal (CRJ) is a peer-reviewed academic journal published by Oxford University Press that focuses on the reception of ancient Greek and Roman texts, ideas, and material culture from antiquity to the present day.

Overview and Scope

• Editor-in-Chief: Justine McConnell (with previous leadership including Pantelis Michelakis).
• Publisher: Oxford University Press.
• ISSN: 1759-5134 (print), 1759-5142 (web).
• Focus: It explores how classical antiquity has been transmitted, translated, adapted, reinterpreted, and reimagined across different historical eras, literature, art, film, and popular culture.
• Cross-Disciplinary: The publication encourages exchange across classics, archaeology, architecture, modern literature, and visual arts.

Related Journals in Classical Reception

• American Journal of Classical Reception (AJCR): Published by Johns Hopkins University Press and sponsored by CAMWS, focusing on the afterlife of classical antiquity in modern media and culture.
• International Journal of the Classical Tradition: Published by Springer, examining the reception of Greco-Roman antiquity from ancient to modern times.
• New Voices in Classical Reception Studies: An open-access journal hosted at The Open University supporting early-career and alternative scholarship.

[QUERENT] what has crj contributed to the study of ai-mediated reception of the classics?

[SYSTEM] To date, the Classical Receptions Journal (CRJ) has not published a dedicated special issue or major body of scholarship specifically focused on AI-mediated classical reception.
While the broader field of classical reception is actively examining generative AI, CRJ’s direct engagement with artificial intelligence has largely centered on editorial policy and submission workflows rather than thematic research articles.

CRJ's Current Engagement with AI

• Editorial & Authorship Policies: Following Oxford University Press guidelines, CRJ’s Author Guidelines prohibit listing AI tools as authors and require contributors to explicitly disclose any use of AI for generating text, creating images, writing code, or translating.
• Pre-Submission Tools: CRJ partners with Cactus to offer prospective authors free access to Paperpal Preflight, an AI-driven tool that checks manuscripts against the journal’s technical formatting requirements prior to submission.
• Indirect Theoretical Groundwork: While not about AI specifically, CRJ has laid conceptual groundwork applicable to machine-mediated reception through its special issues on media, materiality, and temporality—such as Anachronism and Antiquity (Vol. 12, Issue 1) and Failures in Vergilian Translation (Vol. 14, Issue 3).

Where AI-Mediated Reception Scholarship Is Emerging

Because AI-mediated reception is a relatively new subfield, much of the foundational scholarship is currently appearing in sister journals and network forums rather than CRJ:
• International Journal of the Classical Tradition: Published a dedicated special issue in 2026 titled Classical Reception 2.0: Digital Antiquity and the Future of the Past, which directly examines how ChatGPT, generative AI models, digital archives, and 3D modeling reshape the transmission and creative reimagining of antiquity.
• Classical Reception Studies Network (CRSN): Actively hosts calls for papers and workshops—such as Literary Reception and Human Creativity in the Age of AI—comparing how Large Language Models recombine textual corpora against human literary transformation.
